title: Autonomy and PNT conformance and test-and-evaluation tooling: machine-to-machine conformance suites for MAVLink/STANAG 4586/UMAA/FANTOM-style interfaces, DDIL scenario replay, and an ASPN synthetic-measurement generator with pntOS plug-in conformance checks scored against the DHS Resilient PNT framework

scores.rationale: Real and documented but non-existential: vendors re-test per program and find failures late; GAO-21-320SP (2021-05-10, FACT/HIGH) says alt-PNT M&S fidelity is 'poorer' and integrated trade tools 'do not yet exist'; DoDI 4650.08 forces NAVWAR evidence at every milestone. But the pain is capacity and cadence of government assessment, which the government is actively addressing itself (UxSAI AEs 2026, planned pntOS toolkit).

Recurs per software drop, per assessment cycle and per interface family, but the cadence is set by capacity-limited government events (annual PNTAX; SOFWERX UxSAI AEs Jun-Dec 2026; CCA six-month phases), so the felt frequency for any one vendor is a few times a year.

Score 1 because no budget owner for third-party conformance/replay tooling can be identified: the only dedicated open-architecture PNT figure is $17M DoD-wide FY2020-2024 (GAO-21-320SP); the 2026 SOCOM UxSAI Synthetic Data Modeler AE buys EO/IR computer-vision synthetic data, not interface conformance (sam.gov, MEDIUM); NP004 (Phase I OT up to $200k+$115k) funds the vendor's own product, not tooling; CISA's federal PNT guidance creates no funded certification. Not 0 because these adjacent lines prove money exists in the neighborhood.

Vendor-paid B2B pilots need no vehicle, which keeps this above 1. Government-side access is narrow: SBIR is closed to this cap table under 13 CFR 121.702; SOFWERX AEs are U.S.-company events whose T&E is government-performed; a lab adopting a runner has no contracting office identified. Public evidence insufficient for any vehicle that buys third-party conformance tooling.

Schema/contract checking against public ASPN-ICD YAML, pntOS-C, MAVLink and UMAA IDL is straightforward engineering; PX4 SITL replay with link/GNSS-loss injection is standard. The hard parts are realistic alt-PNT error models (GAO says government fidelity itself is poor) and a defensible resilience score (arXiv 2607.05415, 2026-07, shows single-number scores are decision-unstable), which cap the credibility of the core output.

An open-subset proof of concept fits ($60k-$120k, INFERENCE/LOW), but a demo a reviewer would credit needs real vendor plug-ins under NDA, a senior navigation/estimation engineer (fatal-if-absent) and export counsel, estimated $400k-$900k; $250k does not reach the milestone that would justify further capital.

A public pntOS-C plug-in and PX4 SITL run through ten scripted degradation scenarios in CI is demonstrable in 4-6 months. 'Credible' to a NAVWAR/PM PNT reviewer or SOFWERX assessor adds 6-12 months for vendor partnerships and validation of degradation profiles against real logs.

The open subset is genuinely available (ASPN-ICD, pntOS-C Apache-2.0, MAVLink, UMAA ICDs via AUVSI, DHS RPCF v2.0, cisagov/pnt-integrity); public spoofing/MagNav datasets exist (RECALL - not re-verified). STANAG 4586 (NATO-controlled), FANTOM Core and A-GRA are unreachable; realistic alt-PNT error models and vendor logs require partnerships.

The open-standards core and the civil DHS-RPCF product can plausibly be built as unclassified, publicly available software with no clearance or ATO (counsel to confirm classification). Burden rises to CUI/CMMC L2 and possible ITAR-adjacency once the tool is adapted to military-controlled interfaces or handles vendor logs - exactly where the defense value is.

The MVP uses only public specifications, open datasets, simulated data and commercial compute; classification dependence is 'eventually' (A-GRA/FANTOM Core/JNWC threat conditions). Not 5 because the interfaces with money behind them are controlled from day one.

Score 1 because every interface family already has a zero-priced or entrenched supplier: Army says STANAG 4586/IOP compliance test tools are 'available to programs and eligible vendors' (army.mil, FACT/MEDIUM); Army planned an automatic pntOS toolkit (GAO 2021); the ISTO PNT Standards Consortium (Leidos/IS4S/TRX, 2026-06) governs pntOS/ASPN; MITRE supports UMAA (RECALL); SOCOM runs its own UxSAI assessments; CDAO selected Applied Intuition for enterprise autonomy validation (2026-05); Spirent PNT Xe and Skydel AI (2025) automate PNT scenarios; Tangram Flex sells interface verification; DIU Recognized Assessors hold the third-party role for Blue UAS.

Score 1 because there is no evidence incumbents are failing customers in a way a startup can exploit: buyers are building or have just bought their tooling (UxSAI AEs, Applied Intuition, consortium), and the only visible weakness - poor alt-PNT M&S fidelity - is a problem the startup cannot solve better than the sensor vendors and the government's own models.

Open interfaces are well documented and CI/container integration is routine (pntOS-C C API, UMAA over DDS, MAVLink). But the startup controls none of the interfaces, the government/consortium controls versioning, and the two interfaces with growing money (FANTOM Core, STANAG 4586/A-GRA) are excluded from what the team can integrate.

Score 1 because standards are open, the government or consortium can publish free suites, RF-simulator incumbents can replicate degradation profiles in one release, the scoring output is scientifically contested, and no data, accreditation or network-effect moat is visible; the only moat (a lab adopting the runner as reference) is a government relationship the team cannot reach today.

A civil twin exists (DHS RPCF v2.0, NIST IR 8323r1, CISA federal PNT acquisition guidance 2024-03, IEEE P1952 - RECALL) and civil vendors market conformance, but conformance is self-attested with no certifying body or mandate, so paying civil demand for independent scoring is a HYPOTHESIS; MAVLink replay has thin commercial QA demand served by open SITL tooling.

Expansion paths exist on paper (allied navies converging on UMAA/STANAG-style C2 via AUKUS Maritime Big Play 2025-08; civil timing operators; program-office licences), but each interface family has its own owner and free tooling, so expansion multiplies small niches rather than compounding.

In principle a per-drop, per-cycle subscription; in practice the paid market is a few dozen vendors buying a $25k-$100k stopgap until the consortium or government suite ships, and civil buyers have no recurring compliance obligation.

Better than the parents because the open-subset devtool is buildable unclassified by a strong engineer and the civil PNT product carries no ITAR/FOCI/SBIR barrier for the Indonesian founder. Still 2 because both fatal-if-absent roles (navigation/estimation engineer with a real pntOS/ASPN plug-in; autonomy T&E engineer with assessment-event experience) are missing, SBIR is closed to the cap table, and the team has no route to the controlled interfaces or lab relationships that would make the product matter.

market.summary: No requirement owner and no budget: the only 2026 procurements in the neighborhood (SOCOM UxSAI Synthetic Data Modeler and Mission Autonomy AEs) buy EO/IR CV synthetic data and government-performed T&E, not third-party interface conformance or replay; the pntOS toolkit is planned in-house and the standards now sit with the ISTO consortium; civil DHS-RPCF conformance is self-attested with no certifying body; the addressable paid market is a few dozen vendors buying a stopgap - consultancy drift is the base case.

competition.summary: The slot is occupied at zero price for every interface family: Army-furnished STANAG 4586/IOP test tools, planned Army pntOS toolkit, ISTO consortium (Leidos/IS4S/TRX), MITRE UMAA (RECALL), SOCOM's own assessment pipeline, CDAO's Applied Intuition environment, Spirent/Skydel scenario automation, Tangram Flex interface verification, DIU Recognized Assessors for Blue UAS; any of them can add ASPN export or a DDIL replay module in one release, and APIs and versioning are controlled by the government.

feasibility.summary: The open subset is genuinely buildable, unclassified and within $250k - an improvement over the parents - but the demo that matters requires real vendor plug-ins under NDA, a senior navigation engineer the team lacks, access to controlled documents (STANAG 4586, FANTOM Core) the non-U.S.-person founder likely cannot touch, SBIR eligibility the cap table does not have, and a resilience score whose validity the literature disputes.

verdict_rationale: Kill as a venture. Evaluated on its own merits, the narrower form removes the parents' worst defects (no orchestrator, no live multi-vehicle demo, an unclassified open-subset MVP that fits $250k), which is why founder fit rises to 2.8 from 1.8/2.7. But the PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> VEHICLE chain breaks at REQUIREMENT OWNER and BUDGET: no office owns 'third-party conformance tooling', and every dollar found in 2026 funds government-run assessment (UxSAI AEs), CV synthetic data, government-owned toolkits, or the vendor's own SBIR deliverable - the major penalty applies. Competition refutes at strength 5 because the Army states STANAG 4586/IOP test tools are already furnished to programs and vendors, the standards owners (ISTO consortium, MITRE, C5ISR Center) can publish free suites, and Applied Intuition, Spirent/Skydel and Tangram Flex already sell the adjacent products. The civil DHS-framework scoring leg, which was meant to give the non-U.S.-person founder an unrestricted market, has no certifying body, no mandate, self-attesting vendors, and a July 2026 paper showing single-number resilience scores are decision-unstable. Market attractiveness 2.1 is the parents' level; the surviving business is an open-core devtools/consulting niche or an acqui-hire into IS4S/Leidos/Applied Intuition/Tangram Flex, not a company to capitalize with $2-5M.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not applicable (verdict is kill). For the record, the non-venture form that could exist: an open-source pntOS-C/ASPN conformance runner and ASPN degraded-measurement generator contributed to the ISTO PNT Standards Consortium as a credibility project, monetized through 2-4 vendor-paid integration/test engagements ($25k-$100k) with alt-PNT vendors preparing for APEX/NP004-style deliverables, and a behavior-checklist (not single-score) service for civil timing operators under CISA's federal PNT acquisition guidance. Sized as a lifestyle/services business or an acqui-hire path; and better treated as a credibility feature inside a different gap (e.g., the S11 assured-PNT awareness gap) than as a standalone company.
most_important_question_answer: With $250,000 today the two founders should build, first, an open-core ASPN-2023 synthetic-measurement generator (GNSS, IMU, clock, magnetometer, RF-ranging streams under scripted jamming, spoofing and dropout profiles calibrated to public datasets) plus a CI runner that executes any pntOS-C plug-in against those streams and emits a schema-conformance report, a DHS-RPCF Prevent/Respond/Recover behavior checklist and a draft DoDI 4650.08 evidence table, with a PX4 SITL DDIL replay module as the autonomy-side proof. They should show it first to the IS4S/TRX/Leidos engineers who steward pntOS/ASPN through the ISTO consortium, then to three or four second-tier alt-PNT vendors preparing NP004-style or APEX deliverables, and only then to a C5ISR Center pntOS lead or SOFWERX UxSAI staff. The demo must prove that the harness reproduces real plug-in integration failures on two vendors' code under NDA and that a NAVWAR or PM PNT reviewer accepts synthetic ASPN streams and the evidence table as milestone-grade input (the NP004 Q&A of 2026-08-08 is the one public precedent). The customer cares because assessment slots are annual and capacity-limited, failures surface late, and NAVWAR evidence is assembled by hand. The honest answer to 'why can't an incumbent crush them' is that they can and largely have: the Army already furnishes STANAG 4586/IOP test tools, the consortium can publish an official suite for free, Spirent or Skydel can add ASPN export in a release, and Applied Intuition holds the enterprise validation slot. The milestone that would justify $2-5M - a named program office or lab adopting the runner as its conformance reference with a funded OTA, or a CISA/NIST-recognized RPCF assessment scheme that requires independent scoring - depends on decisions the government has shown no sign of making and on U.S.-person staff and SBIR eligibility the team does not have. It fails not on pain but on the absence of a buyer who is not also the builder.
bear_case_summary: The buyer is the builder and prices at zero. No office owns or funds third-party conformance tooling; the 2026 SOCOM UxSAI buys are CV synthetic data and government-run T&E; the Army furnishes STANAG 4586/IOP test tools and planned its own pntOS toolkit; the pntOS/ASPN authors now govern the standards through the ISTO consortium; CDAO picked Applied Intuition for enterprise autonomy validation; Spirent/Skydel own PNT scenario generation; the civil DHS-framework score has no certifying customer and is scientifically contested; the controlled interfaces (STANAG 4586, FANTOM Core, A-GRA) are unreachable for a non-U.S.-person founder and the cap table is SBIR-ineligible. The residual is a few dozen vendors buying a $25k-$100k stopgap.
bull_case_summary: The reference interfaces went public and operational in 2025-2026 (ASPN-ICD, pntOS-C, UMAA 6.0, FANTOM Core mandate, first A-GRA flights), a standards consortium now exists to adopt a reference runner, NAVWAR accepted synthetic ASPN data as SBIR input, DIU has shown it will outsource compliance assessment to third parties (Blue UAS Recognized Assessors), CISA tells federal buyers to specify resilience levels, and GAO documents that government M&S fidelity for alt-PNT is poor. A vendor-neutral open-core runner that becomes the consortium's reference could earn a small, real devtools business and an acqui-hire - and it can be built unclassified by this team.
